newsitem.title: USA: Albright to discuss jet sale with Chilean.
newsitem.headline: Albright to discuss jet sale with Chilean.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is expected to discuss Chile's interest in buying U.S.-made F-16 fighter aircraft when she meets on Wednesday with Chile's foreign minister, U.S. officials said on Tuesday.
President Bill Clinton made the sale possible by lifting a 20-year-old ban on the sale of high-tech weaponry to Latin America on Aug. 1.
Albright is holding talks on Wednesday with Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza.
U.S. officials said another major topic will be U.S. efforts to negotiate a trade pact with Chile.

Initially Clinton was pushing Congress to give him fast- track authority, which would prohibit Congress from amending trade agreements, to speed Chile's entry into the North American Free Trade Agreement.
But recently U.S. officials have talked about a bilateral pact with Chile instead.
On the fighter aircraft sale, two U.S. firms, Lockheed and McDonnell Douglas are competing for the business.

Analysts say resumed sales from U.S. makers desperate for new markets since the end of the Cold War were inevitable after Peru went shopping in Eastern Europe and Chile started looking at European planes if it could not buy the U.S. F-16s it really wanted.
U.S. critics of Clinton's decision to lift the ban fear it will trigger an arms race in the region and undermine attempts by Latin countries to strengthen their incipient democracies.
But regional officials say while the decision is likely to increase military spending in the region, it should not trigger an arms race.
